subject: Re: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — pilot & pricing path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — initial pricing summary

Hi Rita —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As promised, a short summary of the commercial path for the observability add-ons we discussed (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) and a proposed pilot that should get you operational visibility quickly while preserving budget predictability.

High-level offer (pilot -> scaled):
- Pilot (4 weeks): trimmed retention (30 days hot, 365 days cold) + full tracing ingestion for a single service + advanced dashboards access for 3 users. Flat pilot fee: $12,500 (includes one-time onboarding + 4 weeks of retention and tracing).
- Post-pilot commercial options: monthly meter (ingest + storage GB) or committed slab (annual commit with volume breakpoints). We typically offer increasing discounts at 3 commit tiers: 250k / 750k / 2.5M ingestion units.

Key negotiation levers we can use now:
- One-time pilot credit applied to first invoice of the annual commit.
- Retention archival price schedule (we can cap longtail egress for the first 6 months).
- Dashboard seat bundling (3 seats included in pilot, add-on seats discounted if bundled in commit).

Next steps:
1) If you want the pilot, I can get a short SOW ready and loop in finance for DocuSign.
2) Naomi will send a compact pricing breakdown with a suggested concession path and sample invoice scenarios.

Attaching a short sample of the trace ingestion profile you shared; we’ll use that to size the pilot.

Attachments: trace-sample-summary.csv

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@atlashealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Finance Team <finance@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — initial pricing summary

Ben —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we proceed to SOW:

1) Retention buckets: can you give the exact per-GB/month numbers for hot (0–30d), warm (31–180d), and cold/archival (181–365d)? We need line items for our chargeback model.
2) Tracing: is ingestion metered by spans, bytes, or both? We send sampled spans and full traces; need to understand how that maps to a monthly bill.
3) Discounting: our procurement prefers an annual commit if the economics work; what kind of effective discount should we expect at a 1-year commit that covers the pilot usage?

Finance asked me to also request an SOW with clear milestones and an optional clause for SLA credits tied to retention availability. Can you include a stub SOW and a draft invoice so our procurement can review?

If it helps, happy to meet Friday for 30 minutes.

—Rita
Director of Platform Engineering | Atlas Health
rita.gomez@atlashealth.com | +1 212-555-0931
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@atlashealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — initial pricing summary

Rita —

Appreciate the questions; I’ve outlined a compact set of numbers and a recommended concession path below so procurement has something concrete to review. I’m keeping this focused (line-item numbers + a simple annual commit suggestion) rather than a long legal SOW — we can convert to DocuSign once you confirm the numbers.

Pricing (list prices, USD):
- Hot storage (0–30d): $0.045 / GB / month
- Warm (31–180d): $0.018 / GB / month
- Cold/archival (181–365d): $0.006 / GB / month

Tracing ingestion: billed on ingest bytes with an optional span-weight multiplier for high-cardinality traces. Typical mapping for your profile (based on sample): ~1.1 GB/day ingest -> ~33 GB/month. Base ingestion rate: $0.50 / GB. Span multiplier (for >20k spans/min sustained): 1.25x.

Dashboard seats: $225 / seat / month. Bundle discounts: 10% for >=12 seats on annual commit.

Annual commit concession example (recommended to make procurement comfortable):
- 12 month commit at $110k/month committed (annualized $1.32M) gives you:
  - 15% effective discount on storage/ingest list prices
  - 6 months of advanced dashboard seats (3 seats) included for pilot-to-production conversion
  - One-time $25k pilot credit to be applied to first invoice on commit

Pilot-specific terms (to include in SOW):
- Pilot scope: single service traces + 3 dashboards + 30d hot / 365d cold retention for pilot traces only.
- Pilot fee: $12,500 (onboarding + 4 weeks). Applies as a credit if annual commit signed within 30 days of pilot end.
- SLA credits: we can add a clause that provides service credits up to 5% of monthly committed fees for availability shortfalls of the retention read path (examples and definitions in SOW).

Karthik, I’m looping you on the technical approach for the weighted-span billing and an optional flat archival fee we discussed — please chime in with the operational conditional.

If this looks broadly acceptable, Ben can draft a short SOW + sample invoice and route it to DocuSign (HubSpot deal linked below). Happy to take a 30' Friday slot if you want to walk through line-by-line.

Doc: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ATLAS-2027-04-09

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0147
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@atlashealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — initial pricing summary

Quick technical note on tracing billing and one optional simplification for procurement: 

- Billing: we recommend ingest-bytes as the canonical meter (simpler for invoicing). For your payloads we can continue to compute a span-weighted multiplier for internal sizing, but the invoice line will be "Trace ingest (GB)" so your finance team has a single line to reconcile.
- Optional simplification: instead of cold-tier per-GB at $0.006 for archival traces, we can offer a flat archival bundle for the pilot-to-prod transition: $3,000 / month for up to 10 TB of archival trace storage. This avoids metering complexity and makes forecasting easier.
- Operational caveat: the flat archival bundle includes a 24-hour retrieval SLA for archived traces; retrievals outside of that window incur egress fees. We can tighten SLA if you want (priced separately).

If procurement prefers the flat archival bundle, Naomi — recommend we bake that into the SOW as an option B and show both sample invoices (metered vs flat) so Atlas can pick.

Happy to jump on your Friday slot as well to run through technical details.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@atlashealth.com>

Subject: Re: Add-ons: retention, tracing, advanced dashboards — initial pricing summary

Thanks Naomi, Ben, Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail my procurement and finance teams needed. Two quick points: 

1) The flat archival bundle sounds attractive. Please include Option B (flat archival $3k/mo up to 10TB) in the SOW so our procurement team can compare both priced options.
2) Please add a short SLA-credit definition to the SOW (we can iterate on language, but a clear credit band tied to retention read availability will make this painless for legal).

We’re good to proceed with the pilot as soon as the SOW and sample invoice hit my inbox. Can we target Monday EOD for Docs? If so, sign me up for Friday 10:00–10:30am ET to walk through the SOW and confirm timelines.

Attaching our internal procurement template (for reference) and will make sure finance reviews the sample invoice once received.

Attachments: Atlas_Procurement_Template.docx

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Rita
